sourceStatus: Official June 2023 AQA Physics 7408/3BB Medical physics optional Section B question paper and final mark scheme inspected. Source-only references; NOT playable questions, worked solutions or encoded rubrics.
subject: Physics
paperTitle: Paper 3 Section B Option B: Medical physics
paper3Composition: Compulsory 7408/3A Section A (45 marks) plus ONE optional 35-mark Section B for 80 marks. Do not add all optional sections.
markingCaveats: Question 01 requires a coherent comparison: the two marking points must correlate; generic unlinked claims must not earn full credit.

Question 02.1 permits a specific alternative numerical result only when the student's definition of the measured pixel separation supports it; a number alone is insufficient evidence of that alternative method.
Question 02.2 requires accurate rod-versus-cone reasoning; a claim that rods are larger limits credit.
Question 02.3 and 02.4 depend on an official spectral-response graph; 02.4 explicitly awards no marks for a bare numerical final answer.
Question 03.3 rejects an incorrect pressure/force/area relationship even if it produces a plausible numerical result.
Question 04.2 gives method marks for deriving heart rate from several cycles, with a final-answer rounding range; the source graph is necessary.
Question 04.3 requires four graphical annotations; a text-only answer cannot be automatically awarded all four marks fairly.
Question 04.4 distinguishes electrical contact from acoustic impedance; an incorrect property should not be credited.
Question 05.1 is six-mark levels-of-response and requires coherent comparison across three dimensions; keyword counting cannot reproduce the official rubric.
Question 05.2 requires its first mark point before its second can be awarded, and explicitly rejects a conflicting answer.
Official general instructions allow error-carried-forward only where authorised, require contradictions to be considered and restrict bare-answer shortcuts.
